mistake_reason: At step 24, the Validation_Expert incorrectly validated and signed off on the final result “humans” by applying flawed verification criteria and misinterpreting the task constraints. Specifically: (1) They prioritized the 2021 trial’s primary subject (humans) and accepted humans as the intersection without properly validating that the question’s target animal(s) must be those mentioned in both Lagkouvardos’s and Tapia’s H. alvei papers and also present in the 2021 article, regardless of subject role. (2) They dismissed mice despite the 2021 article explicitly mentioning mice in the main text (preclinical context) and failed to adequately cross-check whether mice might appear in the earlier papers under variants (e.g., plural forms, contextual mentions, supplementary materials). (3) The final “negative test” only checked exact words (mouse/mice) and used the absence of matches as a blanket proof, ignoring that the verification step conflated absence of evidence with evidence of absence and neglected alternative expressions or sections. This constitutes FM-3.3 (Incorrect Verification): defective criteria leading to a false-positive approval of an incorrect result and failure to catch the true intersection (mice).
